title: BackUpTrace — Backup Monitoring
description: Single-pane view of every backup source reporting to BackUpTrace. Overview row aggregates all selected sources; below it, one automatically repeated row per source. New sources and jobs appear on their own — no dashboard edits needed.

list.name: source_name
list.label: Source
list.description: Populated from backup_sources. A newly registered source shows up here automatically and gets its own row below.
list.definition: SELECT source_name FROM backup_sources WHERE is_active ORDER BY 1;
list.query: SELECT source_name FROM backup_sources WHERE is_active ORDER BY 1;

list.name: job_name
list.label: Job
list.description: Populated from the events of the selected sources. New jobs appear automatically. Rows with no job_name at all are always shown.
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT job_name FROM backup_events WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) AND job_name IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1;
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT job_name FROM backup_events WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) AND job_name IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1;

list.name: stale_hours
list.label: Stale after (hours)
list.description: A job is counted as stale when its last backup is older than this. Default 168h (7 days) covers both daily and weekly schedules without false alarms; lower it if all your jobs run daily.

panels.title: Success rate
panels.description: Share of events with status = success, across all selected sources, within the dashboard time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'success') / NULLIF(count(*), 0), 2)::float8 AS "Success rate"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp);

panels.title: Failed
panels.description: Number of failed events in the selected time range. Any value above zero is worth looking at.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*)::float8 AS "Failed"
FROM backup_events
WHERE status = 'failed'
  AND source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp);

panels.title: Warnings
panels.description: Number of warning events in the selected time range — e.g. a backup that was stored but whose off-site copy failed.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*)::float8 AS "Warnings"
FROM backup_events
WHERE status = 'warning'
  AND source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp);

panels.title: Events
panels.description: Rows reported to the API in the time range — one per POST, not necessarily one per backup run. A source that re-reports the same artifact on every poll (or reports twice per run, as the Oxidized hook does) inflates this. Compare it with "Distinct files" to spot that.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*)::float8 AS "Runs"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp);

panels.title: Distinct files
panels.description: Distinct (job, file_name) pairs reported in the time range — how many different backup artifacts were actually seen, regardless of how many times each was reported. Much lower than "Events" means a source is re-reporting the same files.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(DISTINCT (job_name, file_name))::float8 AS "Distinct files"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND file_name IS NOT NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp);

panels.title: Jobs tracked
panels.description: Distinct (source, job) pairs that have ever reported. Current state — not affected by the time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*)::float8 AS "Jobs tracked"
FROM latest_backup_status
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL);

panels.title: Stale jobs
panels.description: Jobs whose newest backup is older than their own stale_after_hours, as reported by the source for that job. Jobs whose source does not report a threshold fall back to the "Stale after (hours)" variable. Current state — not affected by the time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*)::float8 AS "Stale jobs"
FROM latest_backup_status
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND hours_since_backup > COALESCE(stale_after_hours, $stale_hours);

panels.title: Sources
panels.description: Distinct sources that reported at least one event in the time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(DISTINCT source_name)::float8 AS "Sources"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp);

panels.title: Current status of every job
panels.description: Latest event per (source, job), most overdue first. "Due" is the age as a share of that job's own staleness window, so 100% means exactly at the limit. The window comes from the source's reported stale_after_hours, or from the "Stale after (hours)" variable when the source reports none. Current state — not affected by the time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT source_name AS "Source",
       COALESCE(job_name, '(no job name)') AS "Job",
       status AS "Status",
       CASE WHEN hours_since_backup > COALESCE(stale_after_hours, $stale_hours) THEN 'STALE' ELSE 'ok' END AS "Freshness",
       (hours_since_backup * 3600.0)::float8 AS "Age",
       (hours_since_backup / COALESCE(stale_after_hours, $stale_hours))::float8 AS "Due",
       (COALESCE(stale_after_hours, $stale_hours) * 3600.0)::float8 AS "Stale after",
       event_timestamp AS "Last backup",
       file_size_bytes::float8 AS "Size"
FROM latest_backup_status
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
ORDER BY hours_since_backup / COALESCE(stale_after_hours, $stale_hours) DESC;

panels.title: Status mix
panels.description: Proportion of success / warning / failed events across all selected sources, within the time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'success')::float8 AS "success",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'warning')::float8 AS "warning",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed')::float8  AS "failed"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp);

panels.title: Runs per day by status
panels.description: How many backups ran each day, stacked by outcome. Gaps mean nothing ran that day.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(event_timestamp, '1d'),
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'success')::float8 AS "success",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'warning')::float8 AS "warning",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed')::float8  AS "failed"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Success rate by source
panels.description: One bar per source, built with GROUP BY — a newly reporting source appears here on its own.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT source_name AS "Source",
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'success') / NULLIF(count(*), 0), 2)::float8 AS "Success rate"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 ASC;

panels.title: Backup age distribution
panels.description: How old the newest backup of each job is. A long right tail means some jobs stopped reporting. Current state — not affected by the time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT (hours_since_backup * 3600.0)::float8 AS "Age of newest backup"
FROM latest_backup_status
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL);

panels.title: Job duration distribution
panels.description: Distribution of reported run times, for the sources that report duration_seconds (Proxmox vzdump events do not). Outliers on the right are jobs getting slower.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT duration_seconds::float8 AS "Run time"
FROM backup_events
WHERE duration_seconds IS NOT NULL
  AND source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp);

panels.title: Last run
panels.description: Status of the newest event from this source — what happened on its last report. "Last backup" next to it answers when that was. Current state, deliberately ignoring the time range. Note this is the source's latest event only: a single failing job among many is visible in the table below, not here.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT (CASE status WHEN 'success' THEN 0 WHEN 'warning' THEN 1
                    WHEN 'failed' THEN 2 END)::float8 AS "Last run"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC
LIMIT 1;

panels.title: Success rate
panels.description: Share of this source's events with status = success, within the dashboard time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'success') / NULLIF(count(*), 0), 2)::float8 AS "Success rate"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp);

panels.title: Failed
panels.description: Failed events reported by this source within the time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*)::float8 AS "Failed"
FROM backup_events
WHERE status = 'failed'
  AND source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp);

panels.title: Warnings
panels.description: Warning events reported by this source within the time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*)::float8 AS "Warnings"
FROM backup_events
WHERE status = 'warning'
  AND source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp);

panels.title: Events
panels.description: Events this source reported in the time range — POSTs, not necessarily distinct backup runs (see the Overview "Events" tile).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count(*)::float8 AS "Runs"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp);

panels.title: Last backup
panels.description: When this source last reported anything. Current state — deliberately ignores the time range. Left uncoloured on purpose: schedules differ per source, so an absolute age threshold would mislead.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT (extract(epoch from max(event_timestamp)) * 1000)::float8 AS "Last backup"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL);

panels.title: Latest status per job
panels.description: Every job of this source, most overdue first. "Due" is the age as a share of that job's own staleness window (source-reported stale_after_hours, or the global variable as fallback). Current state — not affected by the time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COALESCE(job_name, '(no job name)') AS "Job",
       status AS "Status",
       CASE WHEN hours_since_backup > COALESCE(stale_after_hours, $stale_hours) THEN 'STALE' ELSE 'ok' END AS "Freshness",
       (hours_since_backup * 3600.0)::float8 AS "Age",
       (hours_since_backup / COALESCE(stale_after_hours, $stale_hours))::float8 AS "Due",
       file_size_bytes::float8 AS "Size"
FROM latest_backup_status
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
ORDER BY hours_since_backup / COALESCE(stale_after_hours, $stale_hours) DESC;

panels.title: Runs per day by status
panels.description: This source's daily run count, stacked by outcome.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(event_timestamp, '1d'),
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'success')::float8 AS "success",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'warning')::float8 AS "warning",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed')::float8  AS "failed"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

panels.title: Backup size distribution
panels.description: Horizontal axis: backup size. Vertical axis: how many backups fall in that size bucket. Counted once per distinct (job, file_name) artifact rather than once per report, so a source that re-reports the same file on every poll does not distort the shape. Scoped per source on purpose — sizes span kilobytes to tens of gigabytes across sources. A bar near zero means suspiciously small or empty backups.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (job_name, file_name) file_size_bytes::float8 AS "Backup size"
FROM backup_events
WHERE file_size_bytes IS NOT NULL
  AND source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp)
ORDER BY job_name, file_name, event_timestamp DESC;

panels.title: All job events in the selected time range
panels.description: Every individual event reported in the dashboard's time range, newest first — the historical log, as opposed to the current-state tables above. Follows the time picker. Capped at 10 000 rows; narrow the range or the Source/Job filters to see further back.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT event_timestamp AS "Time",
       source_name AS "Source",
       COALESCE(job_name, '(no job name)') AS "Job",
       status AS "Status",
       file_name AS "File",
       file_size_bytes::float8 AS "Size",
       duration_seconds::float8 AS "Duration",
       received_at AS "Received"
FROM backup_events
WHERE source_name = ANY(ARRAY[${source_name:sqlstring}]::text[])
  AND (job_name = ANY(ARRAY[${job_name:sqlstring}]::text[]) OR job_name IS NULL)
  AND $__timeFilter(event_timestamp)
ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC
LIMIT 10000;
